data.title: Consumer Portfolio Services closes $80M securitization of residual interests at 10.25%
data.description:
Consumer Portfolio Services closed an $80.0 million securitization of residual interests with notes carrying a 10.25% coupon.

Key Highlights:

  • $80.0 million of asset-backed notes sold to a qualified institutional buyer, coupon 10.25%.
  • Notes secured by residual interests from four securitizations issued Apr 2022–Apr 2023.
  • Includes an 80% interest in a majority-owned affiliate holding residuals from three securitizations Jul 2023–Apr 2026.
  • Proceeds partly used to fully repay higher-coupon residual financing from March 2024.
  • Monthly payments: interest at coupon and principal as needed to maintain a minimum collateral ratio.

Original SEC Filing: CONSUMER PORTFOLIO SERVICES, INC. [ CPSS ] - 8-K - Aug. 21, 2026

data.title: CDC, FDA Investigates E. Coli, Salmonella Infections Linked to Alfalfa Sprouts
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Health officials are investigating E. coli and salmonella infections in several states linked to alfalfa sprouts, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reporting 55 cases, including two people infected with both E. coli and salmonella.

The CDC and the FDA said alfalfa sprouts grown by Minneapolis-based Everything Sprouts and sold under the brands Calco and Everything Sprouts are linked to the outbreak.

The FDA said traceback evidence collected from restaurants and grocery stores identified the company's sprouts as a source of illness.

Everything Sprouts said it voluntarily recalled certain lots of sprouts and is continuing to work with the FDA, CDC and state authorities. During the outbreak, the company has tested its products daily and hasn't received any positive lab results.

The items being recalled were distributed to certain third-party distributors and grocery stores in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The CDC said cases have been reported in 15 states, with the majority in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

Everything Sprouts produces hydroponic sprouts, with products such as mung beans, broccoli and radish sprouts.

Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com

data.title: Oil Posts Weekly Gains on Simmering Middle East Tension — Market Talk
data.description: Oil futures end the week higher with no progress made toward resolving the U.S.-Iran conflict, and the U.S. planning to tighten the economic squeeze on Iran rather than renew major military action. While geopolitics remain the main driver of oil prices, "the continuation of tensions alone is no longer creating the same price shock as before," Linh Tran of XS.com says in a note. data.title: CDC, FDA Investigates E. Coli, Salmonella Infections Linked to Alfalfa Sprouts
data.description:
(18:31 GMT) *FDA Advises Against Eating, Selling or Serving Calco and Everything Sprouts Brands of Alfalfa Sprouts
(18:31 GMT) *FDA and CDC Also Looking Into Salmonella Agona Cases
(18:32 GMT) *FDA: Epidemiologic and Traceback Data Show That Alfalfa Sprouts Distributed by Everything Sprouts LLC of Minneapolis May Be Contaminated With Multiple Pathogens
(18:33 GMT) *FDA: 55 Illnesses Reported
(18:34 GMT) *FDA: Cases Include Four Hospitalizations
(18:40 GMT) *Everything Sprouts Voluntarily Recalls Certain Alfalfa Sprouts Due to Potential E. Coli and Salmonella Risk
(18:40 GMT) *Everything Sprouts: Recalled Items Were Distributed to Certain Third Party Distributors and Some Grocery Stores in Minnesota and Wisconsin
(18:44 GMT) *Everything Sprouts: No Reports of Illnesses Involving Everyday Sprouts Alfalfa Sprouts Have Been Reported to Company
(18:45 GMT) *Everything Sprouts: During Outbreak Company Has Tested Products Daily and Hasn't Received Any Positive Lab Results
(18:46 GMT) *Everything Sprouts Continues to Work With FDA, CDC and State Authorities
(19:20 GMT) CDC, FDA Investigates E. Coli, Salmonella Infections Linked to Alfalfa Sprouts

By Josh Beckerman

Health officials are investigating E. coli and salmonella infections in several states linked to alfalfa sprouts, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reporting 55 cases, including two people infected with both E. coli and salmonella.

The CDC and the FDA said alfalfa sprouts grown by Minneapolis-based Everything Sprouts and sold under the brands Calco and Everything Sprouts are linked to the outbreak.

The FDA said traceback evidence collected from restaurants and grocery stores identified the company's sprouts as a source of illness.

Everything Sprouts said it voluntarily recalled certain lots of sprouts and is continuing to work with the FDA, CDC and state authorities. During the outbreak, the company has tested its products daily and hasn't received any positive lab results.

The items being recalled were distributed to certain third-party distributors and grocery stores in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The CDC said cases have been reported in 15 states, with the majority in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

Everything Sprouts produces hydroponic sprouts, with products such as mung beans, broccoli and radish sprouts.

data.title: Bubblr Inc. Q2 2026: Revenue $33 Net loss $(441K), EPS $0— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Bubblr Inc. reported results for the second quarter of 2026 with revenue of $33 and a net loss of $(441K). Revenue fell sharply versus the year-ago quarter as the company continued to feel the impact of the removal of its AI Seek app from the Apple App Store, while EPS remained at $0 for the period.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $33 for Q2 2026, down from $712 in Q2 2025 ((95%) YoY).
  • Net income: Net loss of $(441K) for Q2 2026, versus net loss of $(372K) in Q2 2025 (worse by $69K, (18%) YoY).
  • Diluted EPS: $0.00 for Q2 2026 (basic and diluted), consistent with Q2 2025 ($0.00).

Business Highlights

  • Revenue Trend: Net sales declined sharply (approximately 65–95% YoY), primarily driven by the removal of the AI Seek app from the Apple App Store, which constrained near-term consumer demand.
  • Product Strategy: Launched AI Vault on the AWS Marketplace to provide secure enterprise generative AI aimed at protecting sensitive data.
  • IP & Platform Momentum: Continued commercialization of the EthicalWeb.AI search platform, supported by granted patents and multiple pending applications.
  • R&D Focus: Increased investment in R&D and capitalized development work targeting real-time data integration and sensitive-data protection capabilities.
  • Go-to-Market Shift: Scaled back consumer marketing and pivoted toward enterprise channel partnerships and AWS Marketplace distribution.

data.title: Boston Fed Sells Covid Loans to Marblegate
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve Bank of Boston sold all outstanding loans from a Covid-era program that ended in January 2021 to Marblegate Asset Management, an alternative investment firm that invests in credit opportunities.

The Federal Reserve said the 2020 Main Street Lending Program was designed to help credit flow to small- and medium-sized, for-profit businesses and nonprofit organizations that were in stable financial condition before the onset of the pandemic, but needed loans to help their operations.

The program during the pandemic was targeted at businesses that were too small to access capital markets, but too large to benefit from typical small business relief programs. The program made a total of $16.6 billion loans to small and midsized businesses and nonprofits, the Boston Fed said. Those loans were supposed to be paid back by early January 2026.

The Boston Fed said that the program extended five-year loans with an average loan size of $9.1 million. Over 75% of borrowers fully repaid their loans, and the remaining loan participations not paid in full by original maturity were sold to facilitate a cost-effective resolution of the program for taxpayers.

"All equity provided by the Treasury Department under the CARES Act has been returned. The program anticipates a modest return to the taxpayer," the Boston Fed said.

data.title: A $1 Million Renovation Revitalized Their Revolutionary War-Era Home — WSJ
data.description:
By Kerry Barger

This is an edition of the WSJ Homes newsletter, a weekly guide to luxurious properties, celebrity homes, interior design and the housing market. If you're not subscribed, sign up here.

Older homes have a lot of character, but they can come with a lot of headaches, too-especially when they're close to 300 years old. That didn't deter James and Kelsey Shutts, who moved from Georgia to Connecticut in 2024. "Where else are you going to be able to own a home that was built prior to the 1770s?" Kelsey asks, referring to New England's abundance of historic properties.

The pair purchased a home in South Windsor that was once used to confine Benjamin Franklin's Loyalist son, William, during the American Revolution. Sections of the house date to as early as 1695, though it was put through the wringer over the years-it was moved 25 feet back from the road, historic outbuildings were destroyed and part of the original structure was removed, according to the National Register of Historic Places.

James and Kelsey had a tall task ahead of them, but felt as though an ambitious renovation was part of the charm of Connecticut living. They spent $1 million and two years renovating the house, replacing the kitchen's linoleum with floorboards salvaged from the attic and converting a bonus room into a primary suite with a walk-in closet and full bath.

Now planning a move back south, they have put the home on the market for $1.45 million.

An unlikely influencer is taking over Washington, D.C.'s oldest neighborhood. Jamie Peva, a 60-year-old agent with Washington Fine Properties, has sold Georgetown real estate for over three decades, often traversing the neighborhood by bicycle. He shares his knowledge of the area with some 37,500 Instagram followers, most of whom are locals and have no plans to buy or sell real estate-until they do.

"It's the digital version of a refrigerator magnet," he said.

Historic Homes: A Connecticut Property That Housed a Revolutionary War Prisoner

The home, which dates as far back as 1695, was once used to confine Benjamin Franklin's Loyalist son.

The 60-Year-Old Real-Estate Agent Giving History Lessons on Instagram

Instead of using social media solely to promote property listings, Jamie Peva uses his platform to highlight Georgetown's history and local culture.

What's the Deal?

"Arthur" creator Marc Brown and his wife, artist Laurene Krasny Brown, sold their 7.8-acre Martha's Vineyard property for $6.4 million, a year after listing the Vineyard Haven property for $6.9 million. "It was a practical decision," said Marc, who said they have since purchased a home in New York's Hudson Valley.

Want to see more deals? Sign up for our Mansion Deals email alert to have the biggest and best luxury home sales and listings delivered to your inbox.

The Luxe Life

A Virginia couple didn't want their kids "disappearing into their rooms." So they spent $2.8 million building a house with a sports room and swimming pool.

Americans have overwhelmingly opted to sleep in plain, white sheets that resemble hotel bedding. Now colorful and patterned sheets are quickly becoming the more fashionable option.

Free beer got "Brink of War" co-star Jared Harris through the theater door at his university, but acting kept him there. "I enjoyed the camaraderie and being in front of an audience trying to figure out what they were paying attention to."

House of the Week

WSJ's House of the Week brings readers to a European-style California compound with four structures, including a building that houses the owner's pinball machine collection.

"I'm a sucker for color and the grapefruit-colored exterior drew me in," says Mansion reporter E.B. Solomont. "I also really love the old-world finishes, including wood beams and limestone."

Your Home

High housing costs are driving demand for Baltimore's vacant homes, helping the city cut its vacancy rate by nearly a third over the last decade.

Housing starts, a gauge of new residential construction, dropped 12.4% in July to 1.239 million.

A new federal housing law should make it easier and cheaper to build modular and manufactured homes.

About Us

Thanks for reading! Send us your comments and questions, and be sure to follow us on Facebook, X and Instagram.

data.title: US highway agency expands probe into GM pickups, SUVs over engine failures
data.description:
By David Shepardson

The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Friday it has upgraded and expanded a probe into nearly 1 million General Motors pickup trucks and SUVs over engine failures that led to a recall in 2025.

The agency said it was opening an enginering analysis, a higher-level investigation than the a formal review it began this year to determine if the company's fix was effective.

An engineering analysis is a required step before the agency could seek to compel an expanded recall or additional repairs.

The vehicles under investigation are Cadillac Escalade, Chevrolet Silverado 1500, Suburban, Tahoe and GMC Yukon, Sierra 1500 models equipped with L87 engines from the 2021 to 2026 model years.

GM in 2025 recalled nearly 600,000 vehicles from the 2021 to 2024 model years to address engine failure concerns, citing a supplier's quality issues. In many cases, engines failed while vehicles were moving.

GM has received nearly 7,000 complaints of engine failures in vehicles that had the recall work completed while the auto safety regulator said it received 499 complaints.

NHTSA said it has another 191 reports of engine failures in vehicles with the same engine but not included in the 2025 recall.

The recall fix included inspecting and possibly replacing engines as well possible oil system changes.

GM said Friday it continues to cooperate with NHTSA’s evaluation.

The automaker opened three investigations into the issue between 2022 and 2024 then issued a recall in 2025 after NHTSA began investigating.

GM’s investigation last year identified just over 28,000 complaints and about half alleged vehicles lost propulsion.

GM in 2025 said it had identified 12 crashes and 12 injuries in the United Staes that could be related to the issue as well as 42 reports of fire that were possibly related. All of the alleged injuries were minor, the company said.

data.title: U.S. Cannabis Industry Returns to Growth as Rescheduling Looms — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. cannabis operators largely showed a return to year-over-year growth in 2Q, which is well-timed as the industry waits for a wider reclassification of cannabis to a less dangerous drug schedule, Alliance Global Partners analyst Aaron Grey says in a research note. Six of the leading 8 operators reported growth, making it the first time in two years that there has been growth on average for the industry, the analyst says. It's also a meaningful turnaround compared with 2025, Grey says. Growth should continue as store saturation becomes less of a factor for retail trends and wholesale trends remain stable, the analyst says. Meanwhile, the federal government's rescheduling of cannabis could come later this fall, Grey says. The growth and reform would combine to make cannabis companies look more appealing to investors, the analyst says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: FDA Authorizes ZYN ULTRA Nicotine Pouches Following Scientific Review
data.description:
Philip Morris International Inc. (NYSE: PM) today announces that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued Marketing Granted Orders to PMI’s U.S. affiliate, Swedish Match USA, Inc., authorizing the marketing of 11 ZYN ULTRA moist oral nicotine pouch products, including all 9mg variants and one 11mg variant. Additional 11mg variants remain under scientific review.

Today’s action further enhances PMI’s leadership role in the smoke-free category.

“We are delighted with the FDA’s decision to authorize a range of ZYN ULTRA products, which will build on ZYN’s position as America’s leading smoke-free product brand,” said Stacey Kennedy, PMI U.S. CEO. “We look forward to expanding our portfolio of better choices for the 45 million Americans who consume nicotine products.”

ZYN ULTRA positions the brand to further extend its category leadership among legal-age consumers of nicotine products. Like the flagship FDA-authorized ZYN pouches, ZYN ULTRA, with its higher moisture content, is free of tobacco-leaf.

Today’s decisions build on the FDA’s earlier authorizations of ZYN in multiple flavors and both 3mg and 6 mg variants. ZYN was the first nicotine pouch authorized for sale in the United States following rigorous scientific review. PMI leads the industry in securing FDA authorizations, reinforcing its commitment to transparency and science-based regulation.

These authorizations underscore PMI U.S.’s commitment to innovation and responsible marketing practices to adults aged 21+, as the company works to offer alternatives that are a much better choice than continuing to smoke.

The FDA authorized the following products in 9 mg nicotine concentrations:

  • ZYN ULTRA Smooth (commercialized as Signature Smooth)

  • ZYN ULTRA Cool Mint (commercialized as Arctic Mint)

  • ZYN ULTRA Spearmint (commercialized as Fresh Spearmint)

  • ZYN ULTRA Wintergreen (commercialized as Wintergreen Blast)

  • ZYN ULTRA Peppermint (commercialized as Peppermint Frost)

  • ZYN ULTRA Citrus (commercialized as Citrus Zest)

  • ZYN ULTRA Chill (commercialized as Chill Mist)

  • ZYN ULTRA Menthol (commercialized as Menthol Ice)

  • ZYN ULTRA Deep Freeze

  • ZYN ULTRA Wintergreen Chill

The FDA authorized the following product in 11mg nicotine concentration:

  • ZYN ULTRA Smooth (commercialized as Signature Smooth)

EDITOR’S NOTE

  • From the FDA Granted Order: “Based on our review of your PMTAs, we determined that permitting the marketing of the new tobacco products, as described in your applications and specified in Appendix A, are appropriate for the protection of public health.”

  • Pre-market applications for other ZYN ULTRA 11mg variants remain under scientific review at FDA.

  • Today’s news follows a series of recent FDA actions involving PMI’s smoke-free portfolio, including modified risk tobacco product orders for certain previously authorized ZYN nicotine pouches. PMI U.S. began commercialization of ZYN ULTRA in June 2026 under recent FDA guidance.

Philip Morris International: A Global Smoke-Free Champion

Philip Morris International is a leading international consumer goods company, actively delivering a smoke-free future and evolving its portfolio for the long term to include products outside of the tobacco and nicotine sector. The company’s current product portfolio primarily consists of cigarettes and smoke-free products, including heat-not-burn, nicotine pouch and e-vapor products. Our smoke-free products are available for sale in 109 markets as of June 30, 2026. As of December 31, 2025, PMI estimates they were used by over 43 million legal-age consumers around the world, many of whom have moved away from cigarettes or significantly reduced their consumption. The smoke-free business accounted for approximately 42% of PMI’s second-quarter 2026 total net revenues. Since 2008, PMI has invested over $16 billion to develop, scientifically substantiate and commercialize innovative smoke-free products for adults who would otherwise smoke or use other nicotine-containing consumer products, with the goal of completely ending the sale of cigarettes. This includes the building of world-class scientific assessment capabilities, notably in the areas of pre-clinical systems toxicology, clinical and behavioral research, as well as post-market studies. Following a robust science-based review, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of Swedish Match’s General snus and ZYN nicotine pouches and versions of PMI’s IQOS devices and consumables - the first-ever such authorizations in their respective categories. Versions of IQOS devices and consumables, General snus and 20 ZYN nicotine pouch variants also obtained the first-ever Modified Risk Tobacco Product authorizations from the FDA. With a strong foundation and significant expertise in life sciences, PMI has a long-term ambition to expand into wellness areas. References to “PMI”, “we”, “our” and “us” mean Philip Morris International Inc., and its subsidiaries. For more information, please visit www.pmi.com and www.pmiscience.com.

References to “PMI”, “we”, “our” and “us” mean Philip Morris International Inc., and its subsidiaries. For more information, please visit www.pmi.com and www.pmiscience.com.

About PMI U.S.: Invested In America

Philip Morris International Inc.’s U.S. businesses are invested in America’s future and advancing a smoke-free nation. The businesses are committed to providing the approximately 25 million legal-age consumers who smoke cigarettes with better, smoke-free alternatives and to ensuring the products are marketed responsibly. From PMI’s global headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut, and other locations nationwide, PMI U.S. contributes leadership, jobs, investment, and innovation in the U.S. The U.S. businesses employ more than 3,000 people across America and operate product manufacturing facilities, including in Aurora, Colorado, Owensboro, Kentucky, and Wilson, North Carolina. For more information, please visit www.uspmi.com.
